classification.description: Python composable command line interface toolkit

plan.architecture_summary: Click is a Python package for building command-line interfaces with automatic help generation, arbitrary nesting, and flexible parameter parsing. The source code is organized modularly under `src/click/` (with core logic in `core.py`, parsing in `parser.py`, decorators in `decorators.py`, and type handling in `types.py`), and test suites reside in `tests/`. It uses Flit as its build system and tox with uv for environment management and testing. Development tasks, linting, and formatting are managed via pre-commit and ruff.

key_directories.purpose: Contains all Python source modules implementing Click (core, parsing, decorators, exceptions, shell completion, termui, types, etc.)
Contains the comprehensive pytest test suite covering options, arguments, commands, completion, and utilities.
Documentation files and guides written in Markdown / Sphinx.

setup_steps.title: Install uv
setup_steps.detail: Install uv package manager if not already available.

setup_steps.title: Run tests with tox
setup_steps.detail: Run tox (which uses tox-uv) to create virtual environments and run the test suite.

pull_request: Open an issue describing the bug/feature first (unless simple docs typo). Include tests that fail without the change, update relevant docs, and add a CHANGES entry.
code_style: Avoid ternary expressions (`x if cond else y`) as coverage cannot measure both branches. Wrap markdown files at 80 characters. Use pre-commit / ruff for linting.

issues.title: `show_envvar=True` Drops Environment Variable from Error Messages When Using `auto_envvar_prefix`
issues.why: Direct Python bugfix involving parameter error handling and environment variables in Click's core logic.
issues.approach: Investigate how `show_envvar=True` formats or retrieves environment variable names when `auto_envvar_prefix` is set on the context or command, and ensure the derived environment variable name is included in error messages.

issues.title: PowerShell completion mangles Windows paths: arguments are split with POSIX rules
issues.why: Python shell completion bug specifically involving path handling on Windows.
issues.approach: Examine `PowerShellComplete.get_completion_args()` and `split_arg_string()`, ensuring backslashes are handled correctly for Windows paths instead of using strict POSIX escape rules.

issues.title: Invoking a command does not fail on missing arguments
issues.why: Good Python logic issue exploring command invocation behavior and argument validation.
issues.approach: Inspect command invocation handling when required arguments are omitted from within another command, checking whether default or None values bypass argument validation.

issues.title: Improve text wrapping
issues.why: Python text formatting and help output formatting task.
issues.approach: Examine text wrapping logic in `_textwrap.py` or formatting utilities to improve word-wrapping and whitespace preservation modes in help texts.

issues.title: Eager open/close of a LazyFile for error handling can make fifo reading fail
issues.why: Interesting lower-level file handling issue in Python involving OS primitives like FIFOs.
issues.approach: Analyze `LazyFile` eager open/close error handling behavior to prevent emptying Linux named pipes (FIFOs) when there is a delay before reading.

first_timer_insights: First-time contributor PRs can be small, focused changes such as updating documentation contrib lists or fixing well-scoped bugs with tests.
caveats: No explicit DCO or CLA requirements are documented in CONTRIBUTING.md or pyproject.toml, though Pallets projects follow standard open source contribution workflows.
